title: Ethiopian Spiced Roasted Peanuts
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Spiced Roasted Peanuts — raw peanuts dry-roasted with salt, mitmita, and berbere. The Ethiopian street vendor staple — sold in paper cones at every market, bus stop, and street corner, eaten as a walking snack throughout the day.
longDesc: Spiced roasted peanuts are the most portable and affordable protein snack in Ethiopia — the street vendors who sell them from large flat pans on charcoal are a fixture of Ethiopian urban life. The mitmita-berbere spicing makes them distinctly Ethiopian.
ingredients: 2 cups raw peanuts — in shell or shelled
steps: Heat a heavy dry pan over medium heat.
Roast stirring constantly 15—18 minutes until the shells are lightly charred and the peanuts smell roasted.
Remove from heat. Immediately toss with salt, mitmita, and berbere while hot.
Cool. The spices adhere as the peanuts cool.
chefTips: In-shell peanuts are traditional — the shell chars slightly, adding a smoky note.
Add spices while hot — they adhere better to the warm, slightly oily surface.
Stir constantly — peanuts burn quickly once they start browning.
commonMistakes: Adding spices when cold — they fall off.
cookingScience: Raw peanuts contain a high concentration of p-coumaric acid (a weak antioxidant). Roasting converts this to resveratrol — the same powerful antioxidant found in red wine — dramatically increasing the nutritional benefit. The Maillard reactions also produce pyrazines, responsible for the characteristic roasted peanut aroma.
sustainabilityTips: Peanuts — nitrogen-fixing legume. Among the most sustainable high-protein snacks available.
healthBenefits: Very high in protein and healthy fats.
Roasting converts p-coumaric acid to resveratrol.
culturalNote: Spiced roasted peanuts are the sound and smell of Ethiopian street life — the vendor's pan on glowing charcoal, the scent of roasting nuts drifting through the market, the paper cone cone filled to order. They are the most democratic food in Ethiopia — available to everyone.
